name: Baby T. Rex
fact: A baby T. rex was fluffy, and about the size of a turkey when it hatched.
scene: A baby Tyrannosaurus rex standing next to a volcano, roaring, with tiny arms.

name: Baby Spinosaurus
fact: Even a young Spinosaurus had a little sail, and could paddle after fish.
scene: A baby Spinosaurus with a small sail on its back, sitting in a shallow pond and proudly holding up one tiny fish in its mouth, facing the viewer.

name: Baby Triceratops
fact: A baby Triceratops had three tiny stubs where its horns would grow.
scene: A baby Triceratops with a frill and three stubby horns, sitting on its bottom and facing the viewer, hatching from a big cracked egg.

name: Baby Velociraptor
fact: Baby raptors were covered in soft feathers, like a chick.
scene: A fluffy feathered baby Velociraptor mid-pounce onto a beetle, seen from the side, leaping towards the LEFT.

name: Baby Brachiosaurus
fact: It hatched from an egg the size of a football, and grew taller than a house.
scene: A baby Brachiosaurus with a long neck, stretching up on tiptoe to reach a single leaf just out of reach, seen from the side, facing right.

name: Baby Ankylosaurus
fact: Its armour started soft and grew harder as it got older.
scene: A baby Ankylosaurus with bumpy armour and a tiny tail club, curled into a ball, peeking out with one eye, seen from above.

name: Baby Giganotosaurus
fact: One day it would be even longer than a T. rex.
scene: A baby Giganotosaurus with a very big head, chasing a butterfly, running towards the LEFT.

name: Baby Stegosaurus
fact: Its back plates were tiny at first and grew as it did.
scene: A baby Stegosaurus with a row of little back plates and a spiky tail, curled up asleep.

name: Baby Allosaurus
fact: Young Allosaurus had long legs for their size and were quick runners.
scene: A baby Allosaurus with two small bumps above its eyes, sitting up with a huge yawn, facing the viewer.

name: Baby Carnotaurus
fact: Carnotaurus means "meat-eating bull", because of its two horns.
scene: A baby Carnotaurus with two tiny bull horns and very tiny arms, running fast towards the right, seen from the side.

name: Compsognathus
fact: About the size of a chicken, and one of the fastest little hunters of its time.
scene: A small green Compsognathus chasing a dragonfly between ferns.

name: Parasaurolophus
fact: Its hollow crest worked like a trumpet, so it could call to its herd from far away.
scene: Two Parasaurolophus at the edge of a lake, one drinking and one calling.

name: Pachycephalosaurus
fact: The bone on top of its head was 25 cm thick. That is thicker than a brick!
scene: A Pachycephalosaurus charging head-on down a rocky hillside.

name: Gallimimus
fact: It looked like a giant ostrich and could run as fast as a racehorse.
scene: An ostrich-like Gallimimus with a long neck sprinting flat out towards the right, legs a blur, looking back over its shoulder in a panic.

name: Microraptor
fact: It had four wings: feathers on its arms and on its legs.
scene: A small four-winged Microraptor gliding with all four feathered wings spread, seen from above.

name: Protoceratops
fact: About the size of a sheep. Whole nests of its babies have been found.
scene: A small Protoceratops with a neck frill and a beak, standing guard over a nest of round eggs, facing the viewer.

name: Psittacosaurus
fact: Its name means "parrot lizard", because of its parrot-like beak.
scene: A Psittacosaurus with a parrot beak and a row of bristles on its tail, seen from the side, facing LEFT, nibbling a seed pod.

name: Hypsilophodon
fact: Small and speedy, it escaped danger by zigzagging away.
scene: Three small Hypsilophodons running in a zigzag line away into the distance, seen from behind.

name: Coelophysis
fact: One of the earliest dinosaurs, light and quick, with hollow bones.
scene: A slender Coelophysis with a long neck and tail, twisting round in an S shape to snap at a lizard, facing LEFT.

name: Oviraptor
fact: It sat on its nest to keep its eggs warm, just like a bird.
scene: An Oviraptor with a head crest and feathered arms, sitting on a nest with its wings wrapped around the eggs, seen from the front.

name: Troodon
fact: It had big eyes for seeing in the dark, and a large brain for a dinosaur.
scene: A Troodon with enormous round eyes, creeping through the night on tiptoe towards the right, looking sideways at the viewer.

name: Dryosaurus
fact: Its name means "tree lizard", because it lived in forests.
scene: A Dryosaurus standing on its back legs among tall tree trunks, reaching up to nibble a low branch, seen from behind.

name: Leaellynasaura
fact: It lived near the South Pole and had a very long tail to wrap up in.
scene: A small Leaellynasaura with a very long fluffy tail wrapped around itself like a scarf, sitting in falling snow.

name: Maiasaura
fact: Its name means "good mother lizard". It fed its babies in the nest.
scene: A mother Maiasaura bending her head down into a round mud nest full of tiny babies, seen from above.

name: Sinosauropteryx
fact: The first dinosaur found with feathers. Its tail had ginger and white stripes.
scene: A small fuzzy Sinosauropteryx with a long stripy tail held straight up, trotting towards the LEFT.

name: Archaeopteryx
fact: Part dinosaur, part bird: it had wings and feathers, but teeth and claws too.
scene: An Archaeopteryx with wings spread wide, perched on a branch, seen from the front.

name: Dimorphodon
fact: A flying reptile with a big puffin-like head and two kinds of teeth.
scene: Two Dimorphodons with big heads and long tails flying in a circle around each other.

name: Pterodactylus
fact: The first flying reptile ever discovered, about the size of a seagull.
scene: A Pterodactylus hanging upside down from a branch like a bat, wings folded, looking at the viewer.

name: Ichthyosaurus
fact: A sea reptile shaped like a dolphin, with huge eyes for seeing in deep water.
scene: A dolphin-shaped Ichthyosaurus leaping right out of the sea in an arc, seen from the side, heading LEFT.

name: Mussaurus
fact: Its name means "mouse lizard", because its babies were tiny enough to fit in your hand.
scene: A tiny Mussaurus standing in a giant human hand.

name: Minmi
fact: A small armoured dinosaur from Australia, with armour even on its tummy.
scene: A small round armoured Minmi lying flat on the ground hiding, with only its eyes peeking up, seen from the front.

name: Heterodontosaurus
fact: It had three kinds of teeth, including little tusks.
scene: A small Heterodontosaurus with two tiny tusks, rearing up and showing its teeth, seen from the front.

name: Eoraptor
fact: One of the very first dinosaurs of all. Its name means "dawn thief".
scene: A small Eoraptor running towards the right in front of a huge rising sun.

name: Herrerasaurus
fact: One of the earliest big hunters, from before the giants appeared.
scene: A Herrerasaurus crouched low among horsetail plants, about to spring, seen from the front.

name: Lesothosaurus
fact: A tiny, fast plant-eater, no bigger than a cat.
scene: A tiny Lesothosaurus hopping over a log, seen from the side, heading LEFT.

name: Struthiomimus
fact: Its name means "ostrich mimic". It had no teeth at all.
scene: A long-legged Struthiomimus spinning round on one foot like a dancer.

name: Iguanodon
fact: It had a spike on each thumb. The first scientists thought the spike went on its nose!
scene: A herd of three Iguanodons with thumb spikes, walking in a line towards the right.

name: Dilophosaurus
fact: It had two thin crests on its head, like a pair of half plates.
scene: A Dilophosaurus with two crests on its head, rearing up and hissing, seen from below.

name: Corythosaurus
fact: Its crest looked like a helmet, and helped it make deep booming calls.
scene: A Corythosaurus with a helmet-shaped crest, wading through a lake up to its knees, facing LEFT.

name: Edmontosaurus
fact: A duck-billed dinosaur with more than a thousand teeth for grinding plants.
scene: An Edmontosaurus with a wide duck bill and a mouth crammed full of leaves, cheeks bulging, facing the viewer.

name: Styracosaurus
fact: Its frill had a crown of long spikes, and its nose horn was as long as your arm.
scene: A Styracosaurus with a crown of long spikes around its frill and one big nose horn, seen from the front.

name: Pachyrhinosaurus
fact: Where other horned dinosaurs had a nose horn, it had a big flat lump of bone.
scene: Two Pachyrhinosaurus with big bumpy noses pushing their heads together, seen from the side.

name: Kentrosaurus
fact: A cousin of Stegosaurus with long spikes all the way down its tail.
scene: A Kentrosaurus covered in spikes from its hips to its tail, swinging its tail round, seen from behind.

name: Baryonyx
fact: It hooked fish out of rivers with a giant claw on each thumb.
scene: A Baryonyx with a long crocodile snout standing in a river, flicking a fish up into the air with one big claw.

name: Deinonychus
fact: Its name means "terrible claw". It was the bigger cousin of Velociraptor.
scene: A feathered Deinonychus in mid-air with both clawed feet stretched out in front, leaping towards the viewer.

name: Ceratosaurus
fact: A hunter with a horn on its nose and a row of bony bumps down its back.
scene: A Ceratosaurus with a horn on its nose, in profile facing right, jaws open.

name: Plateosaurus
fact: One of the first big plant-eaters. It could stand up on its back legs to reach high.
scene: A Plateosaurus standing tall on its back legs, pulling a branch down with its hands, seen from the side, facing LEFT.

name: Apatosaurus
fact: It could crack its tail like a whip, making a sound as loud as a cannon.
scene: A huge Apatosaurus with a very long neck and a very long tail, next to a tiny tree and a tiny house.

name: Brontosaurus
fact: Its name means "thunder lizard", for the sound of its footsteps.
scene: A Brontosaurus walking towards the right across rolling hills, so long that it fills the whole picture.

name: Lambeosaurus
fact: Its crest was shaped like an axe stuck in its head.
scene: A Lambeosaurus with an axe-shaped crest, head raised and calling, in profile facing LEFT.

name: Ouranosaurus
fact: A plant-eater with a tall sail on its back, which lived in hot, dry places.
scene: An Ouranosaurus with a tall sail along its back, walking towards the LEFT under a big sun.

name: Amargasaurus
fact: It had two rows of tall spines along its neck, like a double mohawk.
scene: An Amargasaurus with two rows of tall spines down its neck, seen from the front with its neck curved to one side.

name: Suchomimus
fact: Its name means "crocodile mimic", because of its long, narrow jaws.
scene: A Suchomimus with a long narrow snout lunging out of a swamp at a leaping fish, heading LEFT.

name: Polacanthus
fact: Its name means "many spines". It was covered in them.
scene: A round little Polacanthus covered in spikes like a hedgehog, looking very pleased with itself.

name: Plesiosaurus
fact: A sea reptile with four flippers and a long neck, which "flew" through the water.
scene: A long-necked Plesiosaurus with four flippers, swimming down in a curve through deep water, seen from the side.

name: Elasmosaurus
fact: Its neck was longer than the rest of its body, with 72 bones in it.
scene: An Elasmosaurus whose incredibly long neck loops once right round the picture, with small fish swimming through the loop.

name: Rhamphorhynchus
fact: A flying reptile with needle teeth and a diamond-shaped tip on its tail.
scene: A Rhamphorhynchus with a long tail ending in a diamond shape, diving straight down towards the sea, seen from above.

name: Albertosaurus
fact: A smaller, faster cousin of T. rex that may have hunted in packs.
scene: An Albertosaurus running flat out towards the LEFT, jaws open, seen from the side.

name: Euoplocephalus
fact: Its name means "well-armoured head". Even its eyelids were armoured.
scene: An armoured Euoplocephalus seen from behind, its heavy tail club raised in the air.

name: Argentinosaurus
fact: Maybe the biggest land animal ever: as long as three buses and as heavy as ten elephants.
scene: A colossal Argentinosaurus walking through a forest that only reaches its knees, with birds circling its head, seen from far below.

name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
fact: The king. Its bite was the strongest of any land animal that has ever lived.
scene: A Tyrannosaurus rex seen from the front, stomping straight towards the viewer, roaring, with tiny arms.

name: Spinosaurus
fact: The longest meat-eating dinosaur ever found, and it could swim.
scene: A Spinosaurus with a tall sail and a long crocodile snout, swimming with just its sail and eyes above the water, heading LEFT.

name: Triceratops
fact: Its skull was one of the biggest of any land animal: as long as a small car.
scene: A Triceratops charging through a jungle clearing.

name: Velociraptor
fact: It was covered in feathers and was about as tall as a turkey.
scene: A feathered Velociraptor leaping through the air from the right towards the left, claws out.

name: Brachiosaurus
fact: As tall as a four-storey building. Its front legs were longer than its back legs.
scene: A Brachiosaurus with an enormously long neck reaching up to eat leaves from the very top of a tall tree, seen from the side, facing LEFT.

name: Ankylosaurus
fact: Built like a tank. Even its eyelids were covered in armour.
scene: An Ankylosaurus seen from above, swinging its tail club in a canyon.

name: Giganotosaurus
fact: Even longer than T. rex, with a skull as long as a grown-up.
scene: A giant Giganotosaurus seen from the front, head lowered towards the viewer, towering over tiny trees.

name: Stegosaurus
fact: The four spikes on its tail have their own name: a thagomizer.
scene: A Stegosaurus seen from behind, walking into a meadow, looking back.

name: Allosaurus
fact: The top hunter of the Jurassic. It swung its head like an axe.
scene: An Allosaurus striding to the LEFT with jaws open, seen from the side, with ferns and a low sun behind.

name: Carnotaurus
fact: A hunter with two bull horns, and arms even smaller than a T. rex's.
scene: A Carnotaurus with two bull horns above its eyes and tiny arms, seen head-on, charging at the viewer.

name: Pteranodon
fact: Not a dinosaur but a flying reptile, with wings wider than a bus is long.
scene: A Pteranodon seen from below, flying over sea cliffs at sunset.

name: Mosasaurus
fact: The giant of the ancient seas, with a second set of teeth in the roof of its mouth.
scene: A huge Mosasaurus rising from the deep with its jaws wide open, seen from above, with small fish scattering.

name: Therizinosaurus
fact: Its claws were a metre long: the longest of any animal ever. It used them to pull down branches.
scene: A pot-bellied feathered Therizinosaurus with three enormously long claws on each hand, arms flung wide, seen from the front.

name: Diplodocus
fact: One of the longest dinosaurs. Its tail alone had about 80 bones.
scene: A Diplodocus so long that its neck stretches off towards the top right and its whip tail curls right across the bottom, seen from slightly above.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
fact: The biggest flying animal ever. Standing up, it was as tall as a giraffe.
scene: A gigantic Quetzalcoatlus with a very long beak, standing on the ground on its folded wings, as tall as the trees, seen from the side.

name: Utahraptor
fact: The biggest raptor of all: as heavy as a polar bear, with a claw as long as a banana.
